analysis:
Two changes.

1. coordinator/api/install.sh adds bind_provider_coordinator and provider_websocket_url, called after bundle install and before Secure Enclave setup.
   - The production URL removes `[coordinator] url` from provider.toml. Any other URL is validated against a host regex, with plain http only for localhost or 127.0.0.1, then written via awk and mv. TOML injection looks prevented by the host regex.
   - The signature pinning, hash checks and paged/fan-helper verification are unchanged. No change to App Attest, MDM or serving authorization (TB-009 and TB-011 are untouched).
   - Residual concern: the written coordinator URL persists, which is relevant to T-040 (installer URL derived from Host headers). Whether the coordinator substitutes __DARKBLOOM_COORD_URL__ from the request Host or from config is not in the supplied source; the next pass should check this in the install handler.
   - If COORD_URL is unsubstituted, bind fails and the install exits 1 after the app has already been committed. This is fail-closed and not a security problem.
   - The awk edit also drops user-customized urls under `[coordinator]` by design.

2. The new coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed and internal/command/devnetseed (run.go, seed.go) add a CLI that writes synthetic users, API keys, providers, ledger credits (including a 'platform' credit) and usage rows directly through the store.
   - It is gated only by EIGENINFERENCE_DATABASE_URL and a non-atomic check that the users table is empty. It runs before NewPostgres migrations.
   - It is new attack surface touching A-009 (the payment ledger), but it requires DB access, which already implies full compromise. If it ships in the production image and is run against a fresh or empty production DB, fake balances would be minted. I did not flag this since no production exposure is shown.
   - The seeded API keys are discarded and the Privy IDs are fake, so no usable credentials leak. The seeded providers use trust level none.
   - seed.go's seedRequests has no overflow bounds on flags, but this is not security relevant.

Coverage: I could not see the Dockerfile or deploy config, so whether devnet-seed is packaged into production is unknown.

findings.detail: Previously, a coordinator URL injected into the installer through Host or X-Forwarded-Proto (T-040) affected only the one-shot download. With this PR the installer's bind_provider_coordinator writes COORD_URL into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml as `[coordinator] url`, after validating only that it is a syntactically valid https://host[:port] (or localhost http). The provider's start, login, update and LaunchAgent all use that URL. If the coordinator derives COORD_URL from request headers (baseURL unset) and a cache or proxy serves the poisoned installer, the victim's provider stays bound to the attacker's host. Later `darkbloom login` tokens and provider traffic then go to that host, and updates are fetched from it. A malicious installer could already run arbitrary code, but the persistent rebinding is new. Fix: require baseURL to be configured in production so install.sh never reflects request headers. Optionally allowlist the hosts the installer may write, and have the provider warn when its coordinator differs from the production default.
findings.title: Installer now persists the serving coordinator URL, extending Host-header-injection impact (T-040)
